The difference between people who read their notes and people who rehearse out loud is not preparation, because both groups prepare. It is where the difficulty happens. If you rehearse out loud, the difficulty happens in your kitchen, on a Sunday, with nobody watching, and it costs you nothing. If you only read, the difficulty is still ahead of you, and it will happen in the room, in front of the person you most wanted to impress. The sentences you have physically said before come out at a different speed. That is not confidence, it is mechanical. Your mouth has done the movement. So say it standing up, say it to the wall, say it badly the first three times, and then say it once more. The fourth one is the one you will use.

End of day one, debrief note. Two good things and one blocker. First, the booth conversations went far better than last year, and the reason is embarrassingly simple: I stopped opening with who we are and started opening with what we are working on this quarter. Three out of five people asked a follow-up question, which never used to happen. Second, the panel was a waste of ninety minutes and I should have left after fifteen, so tomorrow I park anything that is going to be published as a report. And the blocker. I still have no answer on the compliance side, which means the meeting on Thursday cannot close, so my priority in the morning is to find the person who owns it rather than chasing the person who has been apologising.

Somebody asked me what I would tell a person going to their first big conference, and my answer has changed over the years. I used to say prepare more. Now I say something quite different. Get one quick win in the first two hours. Any win. Ask one person a question and understand the answer. Say your own two sentences to somebody who does not care. Because what actually stops people at these events is not language and it is not knowledge, it is the belief, built in the first morning, that they are not going to manage. And that belief is beaten by evidence, not by preparation. One small thing that worked, early, and the rest of the week is a different week. I have watched it happen to a lot of people, including me.
